outcome.technical: _filed_returns.py's _template_reason() over-fired: it matched a template word or an unfilled `<...>` ANYWHERE in outcome.technical/outcome.descriptive, so real prose that merely used the word 'placeholder' while describing the feature, or that quoted a path like `<home>/...` or an id like `<taskId>`, was refused as if it were itself a placeholder - measured against the filed returns of this phase (P125.18, P125.31-0h5, P125.32-0h5, P125.8, P125.29-0h5 itself). Fixed by matching the WHOLE trimmed text instead of searching for a substring: _TEMPLATE_WORD is now a tuple of bare words compared against text.lower() in full, and _TEMPLATE_ANGLE_WHOLE anchors ^<...>$ so only a text that IS nothing but one such token is refused; also added 'pending' to the template-word set per the orchestrator's instruction (P125.11's return used it). The floor check, the identical-outcome check and the testsAdded-empty check were already correct and are unchanged. Added rp15 to test__filed_returns.py: a replay over outcome text copied verbatim from docs/audit/evidence/returns/P125.*/*.executor.json (as fixtures, not a live read of the evidence directory, since a suite's cwd is pointed at scratch space under the sweep) - every placeholder-shaped return (P125.1, P125.2, P125.11, P125.12, P125.22, P125.28, P125.36-0h5) is refused, and every real one (P125.18, P125.31-0h5, P125.32-0h5, P125.8, P125.29-0h5) passes. outcome.descriptive: Submit now refuses an outcome only when it IS a placeholder - the whole trimmed text is a bare template word or a single unfilled `<...>` token - never when it merely mentions one in a real sentence, so P125.18/.31/.32/.8/.29's own kind of return can no longer be wrongly refused.
